name: iam:* narrowed by a NotAction-Deny still yields CREDENTIAL-CREATION (path survives, downgraded)
note: Allow iam:* on * with a same-policy Deny that uses NotAction:iam:CreateAccessKey. That Deny denies everything EXCEPT iam:CreateAccessKey, so iam:CreateAccessKey - a credential-creation escalation primitive - SURVIVES and must still be reported. A NotAction-Deny can never fully cover the broad iam:* grant token (the preserved action stays allowed), so the path must NOT be suppressed; it is kept with confidence downgraded (denyNarrowed) and the limit noting the Deny. Treating the NotAction-Deny as fully covering iam:* would drop the real can-mint-credentials path entirely - a false-safe / false negative (threat-model T8). Regression fixture for the NotAction-Deny-vs-wildcard silent path-suppression defect.
